report.summary: Analyzed chunk 2 of daedalus/structcore/markdown.py: functions _strip_front_matter, slugify, _headings, _dedup_anchors, _classify, _classify_wiki, _content_lines, _link_occurrences, resolve_link; constants and regex patterns; all claims checked.
risks: _strip_front_matter | low | Unterminated front matter returns 0, parsing whole file as content. This may cause YAML to be parsed as markdown. | Add test with unterminated front matter to confirm behavior.

_headings | low | Setext heading detection uses previous line; if previous line was already matched by ATX, setext is skipped. This is correct but relies on order of matching. | Ensure ATX and setext do not overlap in test.
_classify | low | Windows drive letters like 'C:/x' match _SCHEME and are classified as external. This is intentional but may surprise users. | Document this decision or add a test.

_classify_wiki | medium | Namespace matching is case-sensitive and literal. '[[Code:x]]' is NOT treated as namespace; it falls through to scheme test. This may cause unexpected results. | Add test with case variants.

resolve_link | medium | Fallback to case-insensitive matching uses sorted(known_files). If multiple files differ only by case, the first alphabetically wins arbitrarily. | Clarify or fix tie-breaking.

handoff.purpose: Define link classification, wikilink parsing, heading extraction, and link resolution functions.

symbols.name: _WIKILINK
symbols.note: Regex for wiki links: optional '!' for embed, double brackets with no nested brackets or newlines.

symbols.name: _WIKI_DEFAULT_EXT
symbols.note: Default file extension for wikilinks when literal name matches nothing.

symbols.name: _SCHEME
symbols.note: Regex for URI scheme (letter, then alphanumeric, plus, dot, hyphen).

symbols.name: _SLUG_STRIP
symbols.note: Regex to remove non-allowed characters in slugification.

symbols.name: _MD_LINK_TEXT
symbols.note: Regex to capture markdown link text for removal.

symbols.name: _MD_EMPHASIS
symbols.note: Regex to match markdown emphasis characters.

symbols.name: _strip_front_matter
symbols.note: Returns index of first content line after YAML/TOML front matter. If unterminated, returns 0.

symbols.name: slugify
symbols.note: GitHub-style anchor slug: removes link text, emphasis, lowercases, strips non-allowed chars, replaces spaces with hyphens.

symbols.name: _headings
symbols.note: Returns list of (line_index, level, title) for all headings, skipping fenced code blocks.

symbols.name: _dedup_anchors
symbols.note: GitHub duplicate-anchor rule: first wins, later get -1, -2, etc.

symbols.name: _classify
symbols.note: Classify a raw href into DocLink with kind: anchor, external, path, or None.

symbols.name: _classify_wiki
symbols.note: Classify wiki link body into DocLink, handling alias, heading, namespace, vault, type, anchor, external, code, wiki.

symbols.name: _content_lines
symbols.note: Yield (line_index, line with inline code removed) outside code fences.

symbols.name: _link_occurrences
symbols.note: Yield (line_index, DocLink) for every link (standard and wiki) outside fences and inline code.

symbols.name: resolve_link
symbols.note: Resolve a document-relative link path to a repo-relative path using known_files. Returns None if unresolved.

symbols.name: WIKI_RESOLVED
symbols.note: String constant 'resolved' indicating a wikilink outcome.

claims.text: Nested brackets are excluded for the same reason -- there is no unambiguous reading of ``[[a[[b]]]]``, so there is no link in it.
claims.why: _WIKILINK regex '[^\[\]\n]+' excludes brackets and newlines, so nested brackets prevent a match.

claims.text: Default extension for a doc->doc wikilink: a vault is a folder of .md files, and ``[[Note]]`` means ``Note.md``. Tried ONLY when the literal name matches nothing, so ``![[diagram.png]]`` still means the png.
claims.why: The code defines _WIKI_DEFAULT_EXT but does not show where it is applied. The claim about fallback behavior is not verifiable in this chunk.

claims.text: Unterminated front matter: treat the '---' as a thematic rule and parse the whole file, rather than swallowing the document silently.
claims.why: The function returns 0 when the front matter is unterminated, so the entire file is parsed as content.

claims.text: GitHub-style anchor slug for a heading (no de-duplication).
claims.why: The function strips link text, emphasis, lowercases, removes non-allowed chars, and replaces spaces with hyphens. It does not handle duplicates.

claims.text: (line_index, level, title) for every heading, in document order.
claims.why: The function returns a list of tuples (i, len(atx), title) for ATX headings and (i-1, 1/2, prev) for setext.

claims.text: Fenced code is skipped: a '#' comment inside a ``` block is Python, not an H1, and indexing it would put shell/Python comments into the heading tree.
claims.why: The function tracks fence state and skips lines inside fences.

claims.text: GitHub's duplicate-anchor rule: first wins, later ones get -1, -2, ...
claims.why: The function uses a seen dict to count occurrences and appends '-n' for n>0.

claims.text: Classify one raw destination. Returns None for something that is not a link at all (empty destination).
claims.why: Returns None if dest is empty after stripping and angle bracket removal.

claims.text: A Windows drive letter ("C:/x") also matches _SCHEME -- and an absolute local path is not an intra-repo relation either, so classifying it as external is correct, not a bug.
claims.why: _SCHEME matches letters at start, so 'C:/x' matches. The function returns external for any _SCHEME match.

claims.text: Splitting order is Obsidian's and is not negotiable: alias on the FIRST ``|``, heading on the FIRST ``#`` of what remains, so ``[[a#b|c|d]]`` has target ``a``, heading ``b`` and alias ``c|d`` -- the same reading Obsidian renders, which is the point of being format-compatible.
claims.why: The function partitions on '|' first, then on '#' of the remaining target. Alias gets everything after first '|'.

claims.text: ``href`` is set to the destination as written WITHOUT the alias, matching what ``[text](dest)`` puts there: the alias is display text, and a consumer that reads ``href`` (``external_links`` does) must not receive prose.
claims.why: href is set to target (before alias), not including alias.

claims.text: A FIXED literal, matched exactly. ``[[Code:x]]`` is NOT the namespace; it falls through to the scheme test below and is carried as an attribute, producing no edge.
claims.why: The namespace check is `if sep_ns and head in _WIKI_NAMESPACES`. If head is not in the set, it falls through. The code does not show _WIKI_NAMESPACES definition, but the claim is about the logic being exact match.

claims.text: Cross-vault, phase K6, gated on a security review. Recognised so it can never fall through to the note matcher and bind to a local file of the same name; resolved to nothing, counted as deferred.
claims.why: The constant _NS_VAULT is not defined in this chunk, and the deferred behavior is described but not fully verifiable without the DocLink constructor and counting logic.

claims.text: Parsed, carried, counted -- resolved by nobody here. The type layer is a separate module being built in parallel; importing it from the document parser would couple two layers that have no reason to know each other, and answering "does DSSResult exist" without it would be a guess.
claims.why: The constant _NS_TYPE is not defined in this chunk, and the claim about resolution is not verifiable.

claims.text: ``[[#Heading]]`` is an in-document jump. Same reading as ``(#anchor)`` in standard markdown: not a relation between two nodes, so not an edge and not an unresolved link either.
claims.why: If target starts with '#', function returns DocLink with kind 'anchor'.

claims.text: An off-repo URL written in wiki brackets is still off-repo. Attribute, never an edge -- the rule does not bend for a different syntax.
claims.why: If target starts with '//' or matches _SCHEME, function returns DocLink with kind 'external'.

claims.text: Yield (line_index, line with inline code removed) outside code fences.
claims.why: Function yields (i, _INLINE_CODE.sub('', raw)) after skipping fences.

claims.text: Both link scanners share this so "a link inside a fence is not a link" is decided once. Inline code is stripped for the same reason: ``[x](y)`` and ``[[Note]]`` inside backticks are a RENDERING of a link -- documentation about syntax, which this repo's own docs are full of -- not a link.
claims.why: The function removes inline code via _INLINE_CODE regex and skips fenced code blocks.

claims.text: Yield (line_index, DocLink) for every link, standard and wiki.
claims.why: Function yields (i, link) for each match from _classify or _classify_wiki.

claims.text: Standard destinations on a line come first, in their existing order, then the wikilinks on that line.
claims.why: For each line, it iterates over _INLINE_LINK, _REF_DEF, _AUTOLINK, then _WIKILINK, yielding in that order.

claims.text: The two syntaxes cannot overlap -- ``[[a]]`` contains no ``](`` and ``[a](b)`` contains no ``]]`` -- so nothing is counted twice, and a document with no ``[[`` yields exactly the sequence this function's predecessor yielded.
claims.why: The regexes are mutually exclusive by syntax, and the function processes them sequentially on the same stripped line.

claims.text: Resolve a document-relative link path to a rel path in the file set.
claims.why: Function takes document and link_path, computes candidate, checks known_files, returns candidate or None.

claims.text: Returns None when it cannot be resolved -- an unresolved link is DROPPED and counted, never guessed onto a near-match.
claims.why: Function returns None if candidate not in known_files and not in lowered dict.

claims.text: Root-relative inside the repo (a docs-site convention).
claims.why: If link_path starts with '/', candidate is normpath of stripped path.

claims.text: Windows checks out paths case-insensitively, so a doc may spell a link in a case the file set does not use. Mirrors ``graph._resolve_node``'s fallback.
claims.why: The function creates a lowered dict from sorted known_files and uses .lower() on candidate.

claims.text: The four outcomes a wikilink can have. Every occurrence lands in exactly one, and the three that produce no edge are COUNTED separately, because they are three different statements: "no such file" (unresolved), "several such files and picking one would be fabrication" (ambiguous), and "this parser does not answer that question in this phase" (deferred).
claims.why: Only WIKI_RESOLVED constant is defined; the other outcomes are not shown in this chunk.

observations.what: _WIKILINK regex excludes nested brackets and newlines, matching Obsidian-like wiki links.
_strip_front_matter returns 0 for unterminated front matter, causing entire file to be parsed as content.
slugify removes markdown link text and emphasis, lowercases, strips non-allowed chars, replaces spaces with hyphens.
_headings skips fenced code blocks and detects ATX and setext headings. Setext uses previous line.
_classify returns anchor, external, or path DocLink. Empty dest returns None.
_classify_wiki handles alias, heading, namespace, vault, type, anchor, external, code, wiki. Splits on first | then first #.
_content_lines yields lines with inline code removed, skipping fenced code.
_link_occurrences yields standard links first, then wikilinks per line.
resolve_link normalizes link path, checks known_files, falls back to case-insensitive lookup.
